COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
CRLR No. 675 of 2025
Hon 'b le Ash ish Nait h an i, J.
Mr. Himanshu Pal, learned counsel for the
Revisionists.
2. This criminal revision under Section 438/442 of BNSS,
2023 is filed by the Revisionists against the impugned
judgments and orders dated 29.03.2014 passed by learned
Family Court Judge, Pauri Garhwal in Misc. Criminal Case
No.56 of 2013, titled as "Smt. Dipti vs. Suraj Singh", and in
Misc. Criminal Case No.04 of 2014, titled as "Master Tarun
vs. Suraj Singh" (both under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.),
whereby the learned Family Court Judge, Haridwar was
pleased to allow the both maintenance application filed by
the Revisionist No.1 under Section 125 CrPC and directed
the Respondent to pay Rs.3500/- per month to Smt. Dipti
(Revisionist No.1) and Rs.1500/- to Master Tarun
(Revisionist No.2) from the date of filing of the application
i.e. 27.06.2013 and 06.01.2014.
3. The present matter is listed for disposal of the Delay
Condonation Application (IA No.1/2025) moved by the
Revisionists. There is a delay of 4123 days' in filing the
present revision.
4. The grounds taken in the delay condonation application
by the learned counsel for the Revisionists are that the
Revisionist no.1 is an unskilled labourer, earning only a basic
pay of Rs.7000/- per month. From the small amount, she has
to pay for rent, household expenses and her child's school

2025:UHC:11320
fees.
5. Learned counsel for the Revisionists further submits
that while the Revisionist no.1 was trying to save money to
file this case, her brother became seriously ill on 11.02.2017
and was admitted to Himalayan Hospital, his treatment cost
around Rs.10 lakhs and the Revisionist had to spend all her
savings on it. Later on, in December 2022, the Revisionist
no.1's father passed away, which caused further emotional
and financial distress.
He further submits that the criminal revision is delayed
because the Revisionists did not get appropriate legal advice;
the delay caused in the revision is neither deliberate nor
intentional.
6. In view of the above, this Court is of the considered
opinion that there is a delay of more than eleven years, and
the delay has not been satisfactorily explained by the learned
counsel for the Revisionists. Therefore, the Delay
Condonation Application (IA No.1/2025) deserves to be
dismissed.
7. In this view of the matter, Delay Condonation
Application (IA No.1/2025) is hereby dismissed.
Accordingly, the criminal revision is also dismissed.
 (Ashish Naithani, J.)
 17.12.2025
